content.title: Why This Topic Matters
content.description: Linked List reversal and Two Pointer techniques are among the most frequently asked concepts in coding interviews and real-world systems.

content.content: Many advanced Linked List problems can be solved using either pointer reversal or the Fast and Slow Pointer technique. These approaches improve efficiency while using minimal extra memory.

content.title: Interview Favorite
content.content: Questions involving reversal, cycle detection, middle node finding, palindrome checking, and nth node from end often use Two Pointer techniques.
What is Linked List Reversal?
Reversal means changing the direction of every link in the Linked List so that the last node becomes the first node and vice versa.

content.title: Core Idea
content.description: Each node's next pointer is reversed to point toward its previous node.

content.content: Iterative Reversal Approach
The most common reversal approach uses three pointers: Previous, Current, and Next.

content.title: Memory Efficient
content.content: Iterative reversal requires no additional data structure.
Recursive Reversal
Reversal can also be performed recursively by reversing the remaining list first and then adjusting pointers during the return phase.

content.title: Tradeoff
content.content: Recursive reversal uses additional stack memory.
Applications of Reversal

items.question: Interview Questions
items.answer: Forms the basis of many Linked List problems.

content.content: Introduction to Two Pointer Technique
The Two Pointer technique uses two pointers moving through the Linked List at different speeds or positions to solve problems efficiently.

content.title: Main Idea
content.description: Instead of multiple traversals, use two pointers to gather information in a single pass.

content.content: Fast and Slow Pointer Technique
The Slow pointer moves one node at a time while the Fast pointer moves two nodes at a time.

content.title: Most Popular Pattern
content.content: Fast and Slow pointers are among the most important interview techniques for Linked Lists.
Finding the Middle Node
When Fast reaches the end, Slow automatically reaches the middle node.
Finding Nth Node from End
Using two pointers separated by N nodes allows finding the Nth node from the end in one traversal.
Cycle Detection
A cycle occurs when a node points back to an earlier node instead of NULL.

content.title: Floyd's Cycle Detection
content.description: If Fast and Slow pointers meet, a cycle exists in the Linked List.

content.content: Palindrome Linked List
Two Pointer techniques are often combined with reversal to check whether a Linked List reads the same forwards and backwards.

content.title: Pattern Combination
content.content: Many advanced interview questions combine reversal and Fast-Slow pointers.

content.title: Interview Tip
content.content: Whenever a Linked List question mentions middle node, cycle, palindrome, or nth node from end, immediately think about the Fast and Slow Pointer pattern.

points: Iterative reversal uses Previous, Current, and Next pointers.
Iterative reversal runs in O(n) time and O(1) space.
Recursive reversal uses extra stack memory.
Fast-Slow pointers find the middle node.
Two pointers find nth node from end.
Many advanced problems combine reversal and Two Pointer techniques.
